messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int a[3] = {4, 1, 7};
int t;
for (i = 0; i < 3; i++) { t = 0; t += a[i]; }

Question: What is t after the loop?
The student answered: 7

The student understands this correctly: Setting or declaring the total inside the loop wipes it on every pass, so only the last pass counts.

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: sure of themselves, plain English, one sentence of 8 to 18 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["Since t resets to zero every round, the final value comes only from the last array element.", "The loop runs three times, but setting t to zero each time means earlier numbers get erased.", "Because t is set back to zero inside the loop, only the last pass adds anything.", "I put t equals zero inside the loop, so the third element 7 is the one that stays.", "Every pass starts fresh, so only a[i] when i is 2, which is 7, matters."]}

sentences: Since t resets to zero every round, the final value comes only from the last array element.
The loop runs three times, but setting t to zero each time means earlier numbers get erased.
Because t is set back to zero inside the loop, only the last pass adds anything.
I put t equals zero inside the loop, so the third element 7 is the one that stays.
Every pass starts fresh, so only a[i] when i is 2, which is 7, matters.
